sectionHeadings: 104: Every hook reads the exit code the same way
1.1 One tool, two meanings, for exit 2
1.2 The same unperformed read, diagnosable in one place and not the other
3.1 The PR gate probes before it says "stale"
3.2 `SessionStart` reports an unperformed read as one
3.3 One change, three copies, one acceptance
record.summary: Spec 080 taught the `PreToolUse` PR gate to branch on `spec-spine check`'s exit code, and spec 099 taught the two session hooks to read the verb's report. Neither finished the job in the same place. The PR gate maps exit 2 to staleness without spec 063's probe, so a binary predating the `check` verb is refused there with a message telling the operator to regenerate shards that are already correct: clap spends exit 2 on an unrecognised subcommand and this tool spends exit 2 on staleness. The `SessionStart` banner falls to `unknown (check exit 3)` where the `Stop` hook names the binary and its `--version` answer, so the same unperformed read is diagnosable at the end of a response and not at the start of a session. This spec makes all three agree, and does it without adding a subprocess to any happy path.
